findings.consequence: If a pallet jams at the conveyor entry eye, the condition will never be detected. Conveyor motor M-1001 (Y10) will continue running against the stuck pallet, risking motor burnout, conveyor belt wear, and damage to pallets or battery enclosures.
findings.evidence: I/O list defines PE-1002 (X11) as the entry photo-eye, the parameter table specifies jam_time as 5.0 s (T10), and cause-effect entry CE-ST10-03 requires stopping the conveyor and raising a jam alarm if PE-1002 remains blocked for over 5.0 s while running. Lint confirms X11 is unused. In the program, R2 resets M190 and R3 evaluates M190, but there is no logic that reads X11, runs timer T10, or sets M190.
findings.proposed_fix: Add jam timing and alarm logic between R4 and R5: detect entry blockage while running (LD X11, AND Y10, OUT T10 K50), and latch the jam alarm upon timeout (LD T10, SET M190). M190 is already reset by PB-0002 (X1) in R2 and fed into fault coil M199 in R3.
findings.title: Conveyor Entry Jam Detection Logic Completely Missing

findings.consequence: If the thermal overload cools down, auto-resets, or experiences contact bounce, conveyor motor Y10 will restart unexpectedly without operator intervention or pressing fault reset PB-0002. This violates standard machinery safety practices and poses an entanglement/crush risk to personnel.
findings.evidence: R1 uses a standard OUT instruction to drive M191 directly from LDI X13 (conveyor motor overload healthy). In R2, fault reset PB-0002 (X1) only resets M190, leaving M191 unlatched. When X13 recovers, M191 clears automatically, which de-energizes fault marker M199 in R3 and immediately re-energizes conveyor contactor Y10 via R4 if Auto mode (X2) is active.
findings.proposed_fix: Latch the motor overload fault so that manual reset is required. Change R1 to latch M191 on overload trip (LDI X13, SET M191), and modify R2 to reset M191 when PB-0002 is pressed and the overload has cleared (LD X1, AND X13, RST M191).
findings.title: Motor Overload Alarm M191 Unlatched Causing Automatic Restart Hazard

findings.consequence: The stopper can drop while the station is in manual mode, faulted, under E-stop, or empty. An empty release could allow an arriving pallet to bypass the test station completely without stopping for testing.
findings.evidence: R6 triggers SET Y11 unconditionally on the rising edge of release request RQ-1005 (LDP X14). There are no permissive contacts checking Auto mode (X2), pallet presence at stop (X10 / M100), or station fault/E-stop status (ANI M199). In addition, if an E-stop or fault occurs while Y11 is set, Y11 is not reset until T11 times out.
findings.proposed_fix: Add permissives to R6 so release request X14 can only set Y11 when in Auto mode, pallet is present at stop, and no fault/E-stop exists (LDP X14, AND X2, AND M100, ANI M199, SET Y11). Add a rung resetting Y11 immediately if M199 turns ON (LD M199, RST Y11).
findings.title: Stopper Release Solenoid Y11 Operates Without Mode, Safety, or Pallet Interlocks

data.summary: The ST10 conveyor program contains three significant defects: the 5.0 s jam detection logic (PE-1002 / T10 / M190) is entirely missing from the code despite being specified in the parameters and cause-effect matrix; the motor overload alarm (M191) is not latched, leading to an unexpected automatic restart hazard when the overload clears; and the stopper release solenoid (Y11) is actuated without validating Auto mode, pallet presence, or fault/E-stop permissives.
